note: Annual rates used by the what-if simulator. Education only. Update the values and dates when sources change.

options.name: Leave it in the PayPal balance
options.insured: Not a bank account; check PayPal's terms for how balances are protected
options.risk: No growth: inflation slowly reduces what it buys
options.what: Money sitting in your PayPal balance. Easy to use, earns nothing.

options.name: Savings account (national average)
options.risk: Very low. The national average rate is low; online banks often pay more
options.what: A bank savings account. Safe and flexible, good for an emergency fund.

options.name: 12-month CD (national average)
options.access: Locked for 12 months (penalty to withdraw early)
options.risk: Very low, but your money is locked
options.what: A certificate of deposit: you agree to leave money for a fixed time at a fixed rate.

options.name: 3-month U.S. Treasury bill
options.source: Federal Reserve H.15 (3-month constant maturity, via FRED DGS3MO)
options.access: Matures in 3 months; can be sold earlier through a broker
options.risk: Very low credit risk; the rate changes when you roll over
options.what: A short loan to the U.S. government, bought through TreasuryDirect or a broker.

options.name: PYUSD held in PayPal (reward, variable, US only)
options.insured: Not FDIC-insured. A stablecoin designed to stay at $1, backed by reserves
options.risk: Reward rate is variable and can change; crypto rules and terms apply; US only
options.what: PayPal's dollar stablecoin. PayPal pays a reward to eligible US users who opt in and hold it.
